rounds.proof_sketch: Original: (out_features < 1024) ? out_features : 1024. Mutated: (out_features < 1025) ? out_features : 1024. The only difference occurs at out_features=1024: Original: 1024<1024=false → 1024. Mutated: 1024<1025=true → out_features=1024. Both yield threads_count=1024. For all other values: out_features<1024 both use out_features; out_features>1024 both use 1024.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the comparison threshold from 1024 to 1025 in the ternary expression `(out_features < X) ? out_features : 1024`. However, this mutation is semantically equivalent for ALL possible values of out_features. When out_features < 1024, both expressions return out_features. When out_features == 1024, the original returns the constant 1024 (condition false), while the mutated returns out_features which equals 1024 (condition true) - same result. When out_features > 1024, both return the constant 1024. The mutation affects only the control flow path taken, not the computed value. This is a textbook example of an equivalent mutant where changing a boundary condition produces no semantic difference because the boundary value equals the fallback constant.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable. The mutation is semantically equivalent because the only value where the condition differs (out_features=1024) produces identical results from both branches: the 'then' branch returns out_features (1024) and the 'else' branch returns the constant 1024. No input tensor values can affect this since it depends solely on the out_features dimension, and even changing out_features cannot produce different output.
rounds.recommendations: When generating mutations involving boundary comparisons in ternary operators, check for semantic equivalence when the boundary value equals the fallback value. The mutation (x < N) ? x : N → (x < N+1) ? x : N is always equivalent because at x=N, both branches yield N. Mutation testing tools should detect and filter these logically equivalent mutations to avoid wasting testing resources.
